rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 8 October 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🔴 The SFC’s final-form proposed Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds Code amendments are tentatively effective from 1 November 2026 after gazettal. In-scope new schemes would need to comply at effectiveness, while existing schemes generally have 12 months for specified liquidity, money-market-fund and disclosure changes. • 🟡 HKEX is preparing a proposed T+1 cash-market settlement cycle and targets consultation conclusions and implementation arrangements within 2026. Banks with brokerage, custody or settlement roles may need to map cut-off, funding, client-confirmation and vendor dependencies before final specifications issue. • 🟡 The Gold Central Clearing and Settlement System is scheduled for formal launch in Q1 2027, with 11 banks reported as provisional direct participants. This is a market-infrastructure update rather than a participation requirement; prospective participants may need to assess RTGS, custody and settlement readiness. Hong Kong Regulatory Developments 🔴 Consultation Conclusions on Proposed Amendments to the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261007-sfc-consultations-25cc10 ⏰ Deadline: Tentative effective date: 1 November 2026 following gazettal; existing schemes generally have 12 months from the effective date for liquidity, MMF and offering-document changes Products: Authorised funds, MMFs, investment distribution The SFC says it will adopt amended Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds Code proposals, tentatively effective on 1 November 2026 following gazettal. New schemes must comply from the effective date, while existing schemes generally receive 12 months for liquidity, MMF and offering-document changes. The changes cover an alternative VaR approach, anti-dilution tools for certain daily-dealing funds investing mainly in less-liquid assets, MMF liquidity and credit provisions, CNAV safeguards, and KFS classification disclosure. The direct scope is SFC-authorised schemes and their management companies; bank distributors, trustees and custodians need role-specific analysis, and supplementary guidance, FAQs and templates remain to be issued. Actions: Establish an entity-and-fund applicability inventory, accountable owner and transition plan now; map ADT, liquidity, MMF/CNAV, VaR and KFS controls to the final text. Retain configuration, validation, disclosure, testing and customer-communication evidence, and escalate any gazettal or vendor dependency that could affect transition timing. Source: Consultation Conclusions on Proposed Amendments to the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds 🟡 LCQ17: Accelerated settlement for cash market 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261007-daily-exploratory-search-db1220fb15 ⏰ Deadline: HKEX targets consultation conclusions and implementation arrangements within 2026; no final implementation date stated Products: Securities settlement, custody, investment services The Government’s Legislative Council reply says HKEX is preparing with the market for a proposed T+1 cash-market settlement cycle, subject to co-ordination with relevant Mainland units. HKEX targets consultation conclusions and implementation arrangements within 2026 and is considering revised clearing and settlement timetables, longer settlement-instruction hours, allocation and confirmation tools, and a stakeholder workflow platform. It says specifications and guidance will follow, with preparation and testing time; the reply does not confirm an implementation date or participant requirements. Banks acting as brokers, custodians, fund managers or settlement participants may be affected through post-trade cut-offs, funding, client confirmation, systems and vendor dependencies. Source: LCQ17: Accelerated settlement for cash market 🟡 SFST articulates Hong Kong's gold master plan at Global Precious Metals Conference 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261007-fstb-gold-master-plan ⏰ Deadline: Formal launch of the Gold Central Clearing and Settlement System is scheduled for Q1 2027 Products: Bullion settlement, RTGS, cross-border markets FSTB reports that the trial Hong Kong Gold Central Clearing and Settlement System has 11 banks as provisional direct participants, with formal launch scheduled for Q1 2027. Connection to Hong Kong RTGS for delivery-versus-payment settlement is in its final stages. The Government and the London Bullion Market Association are exploring delivery-standards co-operation, contingent on materialisation, and tax concessions are being explored. This is a policy and market-infrastructure update, not a mandatory participation requirement or final rulebook; provisional or prospective participants may need to consider clearing, RTGS, custody and settlement-risk dependencies. Source: SFST articulates Hong Kong's gold master plan at Global Precious Metals Conference Mainland/GBA No validated current-run items. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. No validated current-run items.
